nodes.label: CLI Rework: Simplified Interface Configuration + Onboarding
nodes.norm_label: cli rework: simplified interface configuration + onboarding

nodes.label: CLI Mode-Navigation Hierarchy (User EXEC -> Privileged EXEC -> Global Config -> Interface Config)
nodes.rationale: Kept because the hierarchy - 'go to a specific place to configure a specific thing' - is itself the lesson; cut everything real IOS has that doesn't serve that lesson (no speed/duplex/description, no realistic-but-arbitrary interface names like GigabitEthernet0/0).
nodes.norm_label: cli mode-navigation hierarchy (user exec -> privileged exec -> global config -> interface config)

nodes.label: Phase A: Functional Per-Device Ports + Interface Picker
nodes.rationale: Makes the already-cosmetic port-slot decorations on Router/Switch models functional, ties cabling to specific ports via a Packet-Tracer-style picker popup, so the CLI can later address those same ports as interfaces.
nodes.norm_label: phase a: functional per-device ports + interface picker

nodes.label: Phase B: Interface Configuration in RouterCLI
nodes.rationale: Adds an InterfaceConfig mode and per-port IP/mask/shutdown state; default shutdown=true matches real IOS - 'interfaces are down until configured' is kept as a deliberate, worthwhile lesson.
nodes.norm_label: phase b: interface configuration in routercli

nodes.label: Phase C: Onboarding (Tab-Complete, Did-You-Mean, Help Panel)
nodes.rationale: Bundles Tab-completion, Levenshtein-based 'did you mean' suggestions, and an always-visible per-mode help panel so players learn the CLI without a separate tutorial system.
nodes.norm_label: phase c: onboarding (tab-complete, did-you-mean, help panel)

nodes.label: Phase D: Camera Focus, Floating World-Space CLI, Cable Highlight
nodes.rationale: Scoped to Router only since PC/Switch CLI has no real commands yet. Zooms the camera and floats the CLI panel in world space above the device (instead of a fixed centered overlay) so the device and its ports stay visible in frame, and highlights the cable plugged into the interface currently being configured.
nodes.norm_label: phase d: camera focus, floating world-space cli, cable highlight

nodes.label: Educational Networking Game Concept & Design Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Core concepts (devices, cables, packet flow, CLI, subnet zones, level tasks) are fixed but execution/visual representation is flexible. Keep it simple and feasible - this is a capstone prototype, not a full simulator - but code for flexibility/scalability even at prototype stage, avoiding hardcoded special cases and keeping systems loosely coupled.
nodes.norm_label: educational networking game concept & design philosophy

nodes.label: Manager Singleton Pattern (static Instance)
nodes.rationale: Each manager is a MonoBehaviour with a public static X Instance set in Awake() (self-destroys duplicates); managers coordinate through each other's Instance and public state rather than events.

nodes.label: Input-Priority Mutual-Exclusion Gate
nodes.rationale: DragDropManager owns the single input-priority gate, checking CLIPanelManager.IsOpen, CableManager.IsConnecting, CableRemoverManager.IsRemoving before handling clicks so only one interaction mode is ever 'live' at a time. Any new interaction mode must be added to this mutual-exclusion chain.

nodes.label: ProBuilder Device Prefab Pipeline
nodes.rationale: DevicePrefabBuilder authors device geometry with ProBuilder's ShapeGenerator (used instead of an external DCC app like Blender), bakes parts into Mesh assets, and saves each device as a prefab. DeviceModelBuilder loads and Instantiates those prefabs via Resources.Load first, falling back to the original GameObject.CreatePrimitive()-based construction only if the prefab hasn't been generated yet, so the project still runs before the Editor tool has been run once.

nodes.label: Table Stays Procedural (not prefab-backed)
nodes.rationale: Table's footprint is chosen per-instance by the player at placement time, so it deliberately stays procedural in DeviceModelBuilder.BuildTable() rather than being prefab-backed like PC/Switch/Router.

nodes.label: RouterCLI 4-Mode Cisco IOS State Machine
nodes.rationale: Implements a 4-mode command interpreter (UserExec -> PrivilegedExec -> GlobalConfig -> InterfaceConfig) mirroring real IOS prompts (>, #, (config)#, (config-if)#). Execute(string) returns null for silent success, '__CLOSE__' to signal the panel should close, or output text to display.
